cards.text: King Asa of Judah is gone, and his son Jehoshaphat reigns in his place. Say JEHOSHAPHAT three times fast and your tongue's gonna need a nap. The new king gets to work and strengthens himself against Israel, the kingdom up north.

cards.question: How does the new king Jehoshaphat strengthen Judah against Israel?

answers.text: He stations troops in every fortified city
He sends silver to the king of Aram

cards.question: Jehoshaphat also puts garrisons in the cities of Ephraim that his father Asa had captured.

cards.text: Troops in every fortified city? Nice. But here's the line that beats ALL of it, friend: the LORD is with Jehoshaphat.

cards.question: The LORD is with King Jehoshaphat. Why?

answers.text: He walked in the earlier ways of David
He brought gold back to the temple
He made his army the strongest around

cards.question: Jehoshaphat seeks the LORD, but he seeks the Baals too, just to cover his bases.
Jehoshaphat seeks the God of his father and walks by His commandments, not the practices of ___.

cards.text: So the LORD establishes the kingdom in Jehoshaphat's hand. Me, I spent years establishing myself in the back of a junk drawer, which is NOT the same thing.

cards.question: With the kingdom established, all Judah brings King Jehoshaphat tribute.

cards.text: Jehoshaphat ends up with an abundance of riches and honor, and his heart takes delight in the ways of the LORD. Rich, honored AND happy in the LORD? Somebody get this man a bigger cookie box.

cards.question: With his heart delighting in the LORD's ways, what does Jehoshaphat remove from Judah?

answers.text: The high places and Asherah poles
The golden calves of Bethel and Dan
The idols of Moab and Ammon

cards.text: In the third year of his reign, Jehoshaphat puts a team together: five officials, nine Levites and two priests. I'm not making you learn all sixteen names, friend, because one of them is Tob-adonijah and I'm STILL recovering from Jehoshaphat.

cards.question: Jehoshaphat sends his team of officials, Levites and priests out to ___ in the cities of Judah.
Jehoshaphat's team goes through all the towns of Judah. What do they carry with them?

answers.text: The Book of the Law of the LORD

cards.text: Then the dread of the LORD falls on all the kingdoms around Judah. I picture every one of them peeking over the border, slowly backing away, going, "Nope. Not THAT God. We'll just stay home today."

cards.question: Even with the dread of the LORD on them, the kingdoms around Judah still make war against Jehoshaphat.
Some Philistines bring Jehoshaphat gifts and silver as tribute. What do the Arabs bring him?

answers.text: Rams and goats from their flocks

cards.question: Jehoshaphat grows stronger and stronger, and he builds fortresses and ___ cities in Judah.

cards.text: He keeps vast supplies in the cities of Judah, and in Jerusalem he's got mighty men of valor under five commanders from Judah and Benjamin. Add them up and it's over a million men, and that's besides the troops in the fortified cities. My favorite on the list is Amasiah son of Zichri, "the volunteer for the LORD." Nobody had to drag him in, he just raised his hand, and THAT'S my kind of baker. We'll pause here, friend, because Jehoshaphat's story is just getting warmed up.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 19 quotes "the volunteer for the LORD.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The joke ends with the surrounding kingdoms saying "We'll just stay home today." That gives away the answer to card 16, which asks whether those kingdoms still make war against Jehoshaphat. The setup also rules out the True answer before the baker gets to choose.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later. ... A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The blank in "fortresses and ___ cities" asks the baker to guess the BSB wording "store." No earlier card mentions supplies; the vast supplies only appear on card 19, after this question. The wrong answer "refuge" is also a familiar Bible phrase ("cities of refuge"), so picking the right word comes down to luck, not reasoning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This last story card is five sentences long. It carries v13's vast supplies, a summary of the army count in vv13–19, a standout-detail joke about Amasiah, and the line saying the story isn't over. The bite-sized rule says every story card after the opening card is 1 to 2 sentences. But the approved summary-card example for Genesis 5 in the long-stretches section is four sentences, so the docs don't settle how long a summary card can be, especially when the story-isn't-over line is added to it.
findings.question: Is a summary story card for a long stretch exempt from the 1 to 2 sentence limit, and if so, how long can it be? If the summary card is also the last story card, should the line saying the story isn't over go on its own card instead?
